payload.title: The Empty Ninth Seat
payload.body: Eight lanterns burn above the tribunal. The ninth hangs dark, its chain swaying though no wind touches it. Examiner Safiya's voice cuts through the silence: 'The missing seat is not an oversight.' Master Ilyas watches you from the shadows. You understand now—the examination was never about filling eight seats with judgment. It was about recognizing what occupies the ninth: the absent authority that shapes law by refusing to appear. The chamber holds its breath, waiting for your answer.

page_missing_seat_opt_mastermind.text: Name the missing seat as the mastermind and stabilize the city around the legend.

reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_mastermind_r1: You name it. The lanterns flare, then dim in unison. Safiya's expression softens—mercy disguised as approval. You have chosen stability over truth.
reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_mastermind_r2: The legend becomes law. Citizens will sleep easier tonight, believing the city is guided by a wise unseen hand rather than chaos.
reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_mastermind_r3: Master Ilyas nods once, barely perceptible. You have passed this trial by accepting that some absences are more powerful than presences.

page_missing_seat_opt_reject.text: Reject the hidden-hand story and accuse the chamber itself of manufacturing culprits.

reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_reject_r1: Your accusation hangs in the air like smoke. The lanterns flicker erratically, as if the room itself is unsettled by your refusal to be manipulated.
reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_reject_r2: Safiya's eyes narrow. You have chosen danger over comfort, truth over stability. The examination was never meant to be fair.
reactions.page_missing_seat_opt_reject_r3: Master Ilyas steps forward into the light for the first time. 'Then you will judge alone,' he says. 'And bear what judgment requires.'

payload.title: The Verdict Gate
payload.body: Nine lanterns burn above the tribunal. Examiner Safiya watches you, her expression unreadable. Master Ilyas has already extinguished his candle—judgment is yours alone now. The Sleeping Precedent lies on the table, a precedent so old it predates the school itself. You must choose which theory of judgment becomes law: concealment or dangerous truth, solitude or consensus, fracture or synthesis, letter or spirit. The lanterns flicker. Time narrows to this breath.

page_verdict_gate_opt_diplomat.text: Let Safiya annex the verdict into policy and staged disclosure.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_diplomat_r1: Safiya nods once. The lanterns dim in sequence, each hiding something different. Policy absorbs your judgment without trace, mercy disguised as procedure.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_diplomat_r2: She files the verdict away before you finish speaking. Justice becomes administrative—concealed, efficient, merciful only because it never truly arrives.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_diplomat_r3: The court disperses without fanfare. Your judgment lives in memos and sealed archives, a mercy that no one will ever know was offered.

page_verdict_gate_opt_magician.text: Let Ilyas keep the legend and govern through dread.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_magician_r1: Ilyas's lantern flares blue. The court holds its breath—some judgments are meant to be feared, not understood, mercy preserved through terror.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_magician_r2: He extinguishes the remaining candles one by one. Your verdict becomes legend before it becomes law, a story told to frighten future students into obedience.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_magician_r3: The lanterns burn cold now. Judgment survives as myth, mercy buried beneath layers of dread that will outlast your name and Safiya's policy alike.

page_verdict_gate_opt_corpse.text: Return the Sleeping Precedent to office; let the dead become treaty.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_corpse_r1: The old precedent rises from the table, ink still wet with centuries. The court accepts what cannot be questioned—mercy through absolute authority of the dead.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_corpse_r2: You bind yourself to a judgment you did not make. The Sleeping Precedent governs now, its mercy ancient and unyielding as stone beneath the Silk Road.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_corpse_r3: The lanterns burn green—a color for ghosts. Your choice surrenders living justice to dead law, a mercy that requires you never to judge again.

page_verdict_gate_opt_witness.text: Admit the missing seat belongs to Yusuf who kept arranging gravity.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_witness_r1: You sit where no one sat before. The court recognizes you as both witness and judge, mercy born from solitude that refuses consensus or tradition.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_witness_r2: Safiya steps back. Ilyas bows slightly. Your judgment arrives alone, unmediated by school or precedent—a dangerous mercy that belongs entirely to your hands.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_witness_r3: The ninth lantern burns brighter than the rest combined. You judge as witness first, law second, and in that order lies a mercy neither side expected.

page_verdict_gate_opt_shared_fault.text: Distribute blame and force the city to keep contradiction visible.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_shared_fault_r1: The court fractures beautifully. Discord becomes law, each faction holding a piece of judgment—mercy found in refusing singular truth or unified verdict.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_shared_fault_r2: Safiya argues with Ilyas openly now. Your verdict is the disagreement itself, mercy preserved by forcing the city to hold contradiction without resolution forevermore.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_shared_fault_r3: The lanterns burn different colors simultaneously. No consensus forms—mercy arrives as permanent tension, a judgment that refuses to settle into any one truth.

page_verdict_gate_opt_meta.text: Refuse a single culprit and step outside the chamber's appetite.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_meta_r1: You leave the verdict unwritten. The lanterns burn without purpose now—mercy found in stepping outside causality, refusing the court's hunger for singular judgment.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_meta_r2: Safiya watches you go. Ilyas does not stop you. Your refusal becomes the only true judgment, a mercy that belongs to neither letter nor spirit of law.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_meta_r3: The chamber empties without ceremony. You step outside appetite itself—mercy as escape, judgment as absence, the formula beneath mercy revealed as nothing at all.

page_verdict_gate_opt_forget.text: Let the city forget rather than canonize the wrong truth.

reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_forget_r1: The lanterns are extinguished without ceremony. Tomorrow brings no record, no precedent—mercy found in forgetting, in refusing to make this judgment permanent law.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_forget_r2: Safiya burns the papers before you finish speaking. The city wakes with no memory of your choice—a mercy that denies canonization its hungry, wrong truth.
reactions.page_verdict_gate_opt_forget_r3: Nothing remains but smoke and the smell of old oil. You chose forgetting over truth, a mercy that protects the living from the dead weight of permanent judgment.

page_end_diplomat_state.title: The Narrow Path
page_end_diplomat_state.body: Safiya filed her verdict in triplicate. The court recorded only what could be measured: Yusuf's answers, his time, his compliance. Mercy became a checkbox; justice, a spreadsheet column. Years later, apprentices still recite the formula that saved him—though none remember why it worked, or who first wrote it down.

page_end_magician_legend.title: The Lantern That Burned
page_end_magician_legend.body: Master Ilyas never spoke of Yusuf again. But candidates whisper his name before entering the examination hall, as if naming him might summon protection—or punishment. The School keeps one lantern unlit now, reserved for those who dare question whether the exam tests knowledge or something older.

page_end_corpse_reenthroned.title: The Precedent Returns
page_end_corpse_reenthroned.body: They found Yusuf's answer incomplete by the old standards. The Sleeping Precedent awoke, its dust settling on fresh parchment. No new law emerged that day; only the familiar weight of what came before. Some say mercy requires forgetting—so they buried the question again.

page_end_witness_mask.title: The Ninth Lantern
page_end_witness_mask.body: Safiya's final question was not for Yusuf, but through him. The tribunal had been examining whether he could hold judgment without becoming it himself. He passed by refusing to answer—proving the lantern was never meant to illuminate doctrine, only those who carry it.

page_end_shared_fault.title: The Fracture That Held
page_end_shared_fault.body: Neither side claimed victory that day. Safiya recorded disagreement as precedent; Ilyas called it revelation. The court survived because the verdict contained both answers, neither complete alone. Years later, scholars still argue whether unity or fracture made the law stronger.

page_end_city_forgets.title: The Amnesty of Silence
page_end_city_forgets.body: Peace arrived not through resolution but erasure. The court sealed its records; candidates took their oaths without knowing what came before. Yusuf became a nameless graduate, his examination dissolved into administrative noise. Sometimes mercy means no one remembers who deserved it.

page_end_outside_causality.title: The Court Beyond
page_end_outside_causality.body: Yusuf declined the verdict offered. He walked from the hall carrying neither certificate nor condemnation, opening instead a small court in the market quarter where law serves those who cannot afford its architects. The School called it heresy; the city called it survival.
